text:
Charlie McAvoy's scoring line looks ordinary, 12 points in 17 games with one goal, and his underlying numbers are some of the best of any defenseman in hockey. With him on the ice at five on five, Boston has taken almost 64% of the expected goals, the share of quality chances, 13.4 points better than when he sits. He's playing more than 24 minutes a night against top competition; Evolving-Hockey had his opponents in the 95th percentile last season.

The goals are the part that hasn't arrived. He's shooting 4% against a defenseman norm of 6.4, with one goal on two expected, and his three assists against Washington on Saturday were his first points in five games. Our wins-added measure has him 461st of 560, a reminder that wins added counts goals, not the play that keeps the puck at the right end.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area at an 85th percentile rate for his position last season. Watch the points: when a defenseman controls play like this, they usually follow.
